title: Build a website you can own.
description: The Provelopment Foundation template's own reference site: what it is, the two ways to write a page, and how to make it yours.

sections.lede: Foundation is an open-source website template designed to be understandable, editable and deployable — without locking the owner into Provelopment.

sections.heading: Two ways to write a page

items.title: Markdown
items.body: For straightforward pages: plain text, with a few simple marks for headings, lists and links. The **About** page of this site is written this way.

items.title: JSON
items.body: For structured pages: you declare the sections — a hero, columns, cards, a table, questions — in a small documented vocabulary. **This page** is written this way.

sections.heading: You own your website
sections.body: Staying with Provelopment is a service choice, not a technical hostage situation. The site, its content and its code are yours.

items.title: What this site is
items.body: This is the Foundation template's own reference deployment — the public code, running live, with two example pages written in the two authoring modes.

sections.heading: Built to adapt
sections.body: The **Layout** control in the header switches between the Sidebar and the Menu-bar presentation: the page, its address and its content stay exactly the same. A Foundation site can also serve several languages, several physical Locations and several countries — when a site configures them, their controls appear in that same row. This deployment configures one language and no Locations, so Layout is the only one offered here.

sections.heading: Everything here is in the public repository
sections.body: This page is data, not a mock-up. It is one file — `home.json` — in the [Provelopment Foundation repository](https://github.com/provelopment/provelopment-foundation), which is also where the About page, the styling and the settings live. Change a file, commit it, push it: the site rebuilds itself. The code is yours to take with you.
